States 'some individuals with ASD may develop symptoms later in life'. Symptoms are present in the early developmental period even when recognised later; this framing misdescribes late diagnosis as late onset. Also omits the school special-education route the source gives.

Claims 'genetic disorders like Fragile X syndrome and certain metabolic disorders increase the likelihood of having a mitochondrial disorder'. Also asserts an 'increased incidence of mitochondrial dysfunction among individuals with autism' where the source says co-occurrence appears rare and more research is needed.
